Change the tag to `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` so the tag contract matches the other flusher metrics.

The wait_produce timer tags with "shards", while the sibling metrics in the same loop use "shard" for the same value (shard_tag). Use one tag key, "shard", so queries and dashboards that group by it cover all of these metrics.

issues.descricao: The time.sleep(0.1) added to test_basic to let flusher threads process is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep.
issues.textoGolden: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The added synchronization point `time.sleep(0.1)` added after the second `step.poll()` is neutralized by the test's own `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 15 (same `time` module), so it does not actually wait. WHY: The comment says it 'Give[s] flusher threads time to process after drift change', but the call is a no-op, so the test still races the background flusher thread before `step.join()` and is liable to be flaky / to not exercise the intended post-drift flush path. HOW: Use a non-monkeypatched wait (e.g. capture the real sleep before patching, or use the flusher's thread/process join, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a real timeout).

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait: line 15 of the same test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces `sleep` on the global `time` module, so this call (and the flusher's own `time.sleep`) is a no-op. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is therefore false — the call returns instantly and provides no synchronisation, so the test does not actually wait for the flusher to process after the drift change. Either synchronise on a real condition (e.g. wait until the expected message is produced) or, if the original `time.sleep` is needed here, patch a module-scoped reference instead of the global `time.sleep`.

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so nothing waits for the flusher threads before `step.join()` and the `messages` assertion. Replace it with a condition-based wait, such as polling until `messages` is non-empty with a deadline. Use the real sleep saved before patching if a delay is needed.

issues.descricao: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
issues.textoGolden: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

comentarios.texto: The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard does not match the SpawnProcess instances created by self.mp_context.Process. When a worker hangs, the guard skips kill() and the replacement starts while the original worker remains alive, allowing overlapping flushing of the same shards if the original resumes and leaking hung workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or self.mp_context.Process, and kill and join the old worker before replacing it.

The workers are created with get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances; these are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class). Consequently this guard skips kill() for actual production workers. When a worker hangs, the replacement starts while the original remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the spawn-context Process class for the check, and fix the identical check in join() so shutdown also terminates surviving workers.

Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the separate multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this guard skips kill() for production workers. When a live worker exceeds max-unhealthy-seconds, the code starts a replacement and overwrites its handle while the original is still running. If the original resumes, both workers flush the same shards, and repeated hangs can exceed the configured process limit. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or explicitly distinguish threads) and stop the old worker before replacing it.

issues.descricao: join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.
issues.textoGolden: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

comentarios.texto: join() breaks out of the worker loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping cleanup for every remaining worker. If next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier worker exhausts it, remaining flushers can continue running after shutdown or partition reassignment. Use the deadline only to limit waiting and still terminate and reap every remaining process.

Do not break out of worker cleanup when the join deadline expires. If the first worker consumes the timeout, the next iteration breaks before terminating that worker or any subsequent workers. They may still be blocked in Redis or producer calls despite the shared stopped flag, leaving old workers running after strategy shutdown/reassignment. Apply the deadline only to waiting, and perform termination cleanup for every worker regardless of remaining time (using a type check that recognizes spawn-context workers).
join() waits for processes sequentially against a single shared deadline and breaks without terminating remaining processes once it expires, leaking them.

issues.descricao: The SpanFlusher docstring says it creates one process per shard, but shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

comentarios.texto: The docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the code at lines 60-66 shares shards across a capped number of processes (num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)); each shard assigned via i % self.num_processes). With the new --flusher-processes default of 1, a single process handles every shard, so the documented contract is the opposite of the behaviour this PR introduces (confirmed by test_flusher_processes_limit, which asserts 4 shards served by 2 processes). Update the docstring to say shards are distributed across up to max_processes flusher processes.

The new docstring says this creates one process per shard, but workers are capped by max_processes and shards are distributed among them. In particular, the CLI default of 1 means all assigned shards share one process. Describe capped workers with potentially multiple shards per worker so callers do not rely on per-shard process isolation.

The docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard', but the number of processes is capped by max_processes (--flusher-processes), and shards are shared across processes via i % num_processes. Reword it to say that shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

issues.descricao: max_processes uses a truthiness fallback, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes one process per shard instead of being rejected.

comentarios.texto: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats a falsy value as 'not provided'. The new `--flusher-processes` click option is `type=int`, so a user can pass `0`; that legitimate-but-falsy value is discarded and the flusher silently spawns one process per shard instead of honoring the requested limit. Use an explicit None check, e.g. `self.max_processes = max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (and validate/reject 0 upstream).

An explicit max_processes=0 is treated as an omitted limit by `or`, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` starts one process per assigned shard instead of respecting or rejecting the supplied zero limit. The CLI accepts zero as an integer and the factory forwards it unchanged. Default only when max_processes is None, and explicitly validate that supplied process limits are positive so zero cannot silently enable potentially many workers.

`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses a truthiness test, so an explicit 0 is treated as 'unset' and silently expands to one process per shard. Use `max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and reject values below 1.

issues.descricao: A negative --flusher-processes value is not validated and makes SpanFlusher construction fail with KeyError.

comentarios.texto: `flusher_processes` is not validated to be >= 1. `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` lets a negative value through (it is truthy), so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative and `range(self.num_processes)` is empty, leaving `process_to_shards_map` as `{}`. The following loop computes `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, which for any negative divisor is 0, so `self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard)` raises KeyError and the consumer fails to construct. Since `flusher_processes` is exposed as an int CLI option (`--flusher-processes`), a negative value is reachable from configuration. Guard with `max(1, self.num_processes)` / validate the input.
negative max_processes flows through `or` guard into min() -> empty map -> KeyError on i % num_processes; empty assigned_shards yields zero processes.

issues.descricao: submit() queries cluster-wide Redis memory once per flusher buffer, repeating identical INFO calls per process on every submit.

comentarios.texto: The new loop calls get_memory_info() once per flusher buffer even though SpansBuffer.get_memory_info delegates to iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client), which fetches INFO for the entire Redis cluster regardless of assigned_shards. With P flusher processes and memory backpressure enabled, each submitted batch now performs P identical cluster-wide memory queries on the consumer thread instead of one, increasing Redis traffic and blocking ingestion. Fetch cluster memory information once from a single buffer.
submit() loop calls buffer.get_memory_info() per flusher but each call is cluster-wide from same client, repeating identical INFO N× per submit.

issues.descricao: _create_process_for_shard is added but never called.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is newly added but has no caller anywhere (grep for `_create_process_for_shard(` finds only its definition); the restart path actually used is `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. WHY: This is dead code that indicates the intended per-shard restart wiring was left incomplete — any future caller relying on restarting only the process owning a given shard will silently do nothing, and it is confusing which restart path is authoritative. HOW: Remove `_create_process_for_shard`, or wire it into `_ensure_processes_alive` if per-shard restart was intended.

issues.descricao: test_flusher_processes_limit counts assigned shards instead of checking that each shard is assigned exactly once.

comentarios.texto: The assertion counts shard entries rather than verifying shard assignment. A broken distribution such as {0: [0, 1], 1: [0, 1]} still passes all assertions in this test while shards 2 and 3 are never flushed. Assert that the flattened mapping contains exactly the expected assigned shards, with no duplicates (and verify each worker's shard buffer uses that mapping), rather than only asserting a total of four.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` (so it is identical to `start`), and uses `find` so any single working-hour entry that excludes the slot rejects it. It also compares UTC `day()` and UTC minutes against working hours that are in the organizer's timezone. WHY: A schedule with split ranges on one day (for example 9-12 and 14-17) is a normal case. The slot at 14:00 is outside the 9-12 entry, so it is rejected and a valid slot disappears for fixed and loose hosts. A slot that starts inside the hours but ends after closing is accepted. Non-UTC organizers get wrong day and time comparisons. HOW: Use slotEndTime for `end`. Mark the slot unavailable only if NO working-hour entry for that day contains [start, end]. Convert the slot into the organizer timezone, or use UTC-serialized working hours consistently, before comparing day and minutes.

WHAT: The date-override check compares two dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false. It also tests only `slotStartTime.isAfter(override end)` rather than the slot end, and the offset `utcOffset * -1` is applied to a UTC-based date. WHY: A slot that starts before the override end and finishes after it passes as available, so a fixed host can be booked outside their override window. The `===` branch, meant for zero-length overrides (a fully blocked day), never fires, so such days are not blocked here. HOW: Use `.isSame()`, compare `slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`, and compute the override boundaries in a way that is consistent with how override start/end are stored.

WHAT: The override start and end are shifted by the timezone offset difference and then reduced to minutes-of-day independently, with no handling of midnight wrap. The `activeOverrides` filter still uses the unshifted UTC start. `override.timeZone` may be undefined, in which case `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the default or guessed zone. WHY: For invitee and organizer zones far apart, the shifted start can land on the previous or next day. startTime is then greater than endTime, or the override falls on the wrong invitee day, so slots are wrong or missing. HOW: Handle day rollover, either by clamping or splitting the range. Select active overrides after applying the offset, and guard against a missing `override.timeZone`.

WHAT: `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the `busy.every(...)` check runs. WHY: any slot on a date with an override skips busy-time, booking and buffer conflict checks, so a host with a date override can be double-booked and calendar conflicts on that day are ignored. HOW: remove the early return and fall through to the busy check. Skip only the working-hours check when an override exists.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that start within working hours but end after them are accepted.
issues.textoGolden: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — an exact duplicate of `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. WHY: the working-hours upper-bound test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore compares the slot START against the working-day end, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) overruns `workingHour.endTime` is never filtered and is reported as available, allowing bookings outside the host's working hours. HOW: compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();`.

`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so it always equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check is identical to the `start` check and never catches a slot that starts within working hours but ends past them. Use `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` for `end`.

`end` is computed identically to `start` (both from slotStartTime), so the check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` can never reject a slot on the upper bound. A slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is wrongly considered available; derive `end` from slotEndTime instead.

issues.descricao: The date-override check compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so zero-length (day off) overrides are never detected.
issues.textoGolden: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

comentarios.texto: This compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with `===` (reference equality), which is always false, so a zero-length override (start equal to end, whole day blocked) never returns true here. Compare timestamps, e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))`.

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate dayjs object references, so `===` is always false. The zero-length date-override branch is dead code and such an override is never recognised as covering the day; compare values (e.g. .isSame() or .valueOf() === .valueOf()) instead.

The equality check compares two separately created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length/closed-day rejection is unreachable, and a slot beginning exactly at that instant can reach the dateOverrideExist success return. Compare timestamps or use isSame instead.

issues.descricao: When a date override exists for the day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times, so slots overlapping existing bookings are reported available.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: when `dateOverrideExist` is true the function returns `true` before running the `busy.every(...)` check at the end. WHY: on any day that has a matching date override, a slot inside the override is reported available without checking the host's existing bookings (`busy` is spread via `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`), so a fixed/loose host who already has a booking during the override window is still shown as free — enabling double-booking. HOW: do not return early here; fall through so the override branch only decides whether the slot is inside the override window, and let the existing `busy` evaluation decide availability (e.g. `if (dateOverrideExist) { /* within override, still check busy */ } else { /* fall through to busy */ }`).

The new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits the `busy` conflict check (and the workingHours check) for any slot that falls inside a date override window. Every caller of `checkIfIsAvailable` previously counted on it returning false for a slot that overlaps an existing booking; on days covered by a date override that guarantee is gone, so slots conflicting with the user's real bookings are now reported as available and can be double-booked. The override branch should let control fall through to the `busy.every(...)` check (returning true only for the availability-window part) instead of returning early.

A matching date override returns true before checking busy periods. Both fixed-host and loose-host callers pass calendar and booking conflicts in busy, so a host with an override is offered even when an existing booking overlaps the slot. Continue to the busy checks after validating the override instead of returning true.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for the weekday excludes it, so split schedules (e.g. morning and afternoon) reject all slots.

comentarios.texto: The working-hours predicate rejects a slot if any interval on its weekday does not contain it. A split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 therefore loses every slot, since each valid slot lies outside the other interval. Require at least one matching interval to contain the full event instead of finding an interval that excludes it.

This search rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours window on that weekday. With split hours of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon window. Check for containment in at least one applicable window rather than finding any window that excludes the slot.

WHAT: Outside-working-hours test uses workingHours.find() returning true if ANY entry rejects the slot. WHY: With split schedules (two entries same weekday, e.g. morning+afternoon) a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon entry, find() matches and the slot is wrongly rejected as outside hours. HOW: Invert logic to accept if ANY entry contains the slot (e.g. !workingHours.some(entry contains slot) => outside).

issues.descricao: The date-override bound compares the slot start, not the slot end, with the override end, so slots extending past the override are accepted.

comentarios.texto: The override bounds reject only non-overlapping slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside an override. A fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability, despite being unavailable for its final half hour. Accept only when at least one override contains both slotStartTime and slotEndTime; this also avoids rejecting a slot merely because another interval on the same date does not overlap it.

The upper bound checks whether slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override end but finishes after it is treated as available. Compare slotEndTime with the override end using isAfter, so the slot must fit entirely inside the override.

issues.descricao: The override timezone conversion keeps only hour and minute, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone become inverted ranges or are applied to the wrong day.

comentarios.texto: Timezone conversion takes only hour and minute, discarding day rollover and turning intervals crossing attendee midnight into reversed ranges. A UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30, which buildSlots skips because start is greater than end, removing valid availability. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval across attendee-day boundaries before building slots.

WHAT: activeOverrides are filtered by UTC day (line 206-207) before the invitee/organizer offset is applied (lines 212-224), and shifted hours are not re-bucketed across midnight. WHY: An override that shifts to the previous/next calendar day in the invitee timezone is dropped from the wrong day or applied to the wrong day, so slots show open when the organizer is off (and vice versa). HOW: Filter/bucket overrides in the invitee-local date after applying the offset, or emit split entries spanning two invitee days.

issues.descricao: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

comentarios.texto: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

issues.descricao: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

The override day is computed with local-time dayjs(date.start) while the slot day is formatted in UTC, so on a server not running in UTC overrides near midnight are applied to the wrong day or skipped.
With several date-override ranges on the same day, a slot is rejected as soon as it falls outside any one of them, so slots inside the other ranges become unavailable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, `dispatch` returns `pipeline.next_step()` before comparing `github_authenticated_user` against the installer. WHY: The user-match check is skipped on this path, so an attacker can link any installation_id whose Integration row is not yet created. The Integration row is created by the installation webhook, so a webhook delay or a missing row opens this path. HOW: Fail closed here, or verify the installation's sender or account through the GitHub API (for example a user-token check of `/user/installations`) before advancing.

WHAT: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is indexed unconditionally. WHY: `build_integration` only stores `sender` when it is present in state, so existing or webhook-less Integrations lack the key. The install then fails with an unhandled KeyError (HTTP 500) instead of the error page. HOW: Read it defensively with `.get` and treat a missing sender as a validation failure.

issues.descricao: error() calls _(error_short) on a variable and callers pass plain literals, so the short error strings are no longer extractable for translation.

comentarios.texto: The helper calls `_(error_short)` on a variable, and callers pass plain string literals. The translation extractor cannot see these strings, so the short error messages sent to the user are no longer translatable; the old code wrapped the literals directly in `_()`. Mark the literals with gettext_lazy at the call sites and the default, and pass them through without wrapping again.

error_short strings bypass translation extraction: _(error_short) uses a variable so makemessages cannot collect them. Wrap literals at definition/call sites, e.g. error_short=_("Invalid installation request.") and pass _("...") literals, then use data error value directly without re-wrapping.

Translate the short-message literals at their definition/call sites instead of calling `_(error_short)` on a variable. Django's message extraction cannot extract the default `"Invalid installation request."` or the plain-string arguments at the two call sites from this dynamic gettext invocation. The existing pending-deletion and already-installed messages previously appeared directly inside `_()`; this refactor removes their extraction sites, and the new default message cannot enter translation catalogs. Use a translated default and translated arguments, then place `error_short` directly into the payload so these user-facing errors remain localizable.

issues.descricao: The org parameter of error()/get_document_origin is actually the active-organization context, not an Organization, so the name is misleading.

comentarios.texto: The parameter is named `org` but the code treats it as the pipeline's active-organization context: it dereferences `org.organization` and every caller (error() and the GitHubInstallation sites) passes `self.active_organization`, not an Organization. The name misstates the argument's type/contract — a caller following the name and passing a real Organization would hit AttributeError on `.organization`. Rename the parameter (e.g. `active_organization`) and correct the corresponding name in `error()` at line 131 so the two signatures match what is actually passed.

issues.descricao: The GitHub OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a static md5 of the pipeline view names, instead of a per-attempt random nonce, so it gives no CSRF protection.
issues.textoGolden: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

comentarios.texto: The OAuth state is pipeline.signature, which Pipeline.__init__ computes solely from pipeline view class names and therefore shares across all users and installation attempts. An attacker can obtain an OAuth code for their own GitHub account and send a callback using this known state to a victim with an active installation pipeline, binding the attacker's GitHub identity to the victim's flow instead of rejecting the forged callback. Generate a random per-attempt nonce, store it in pipeline state, and validate that nonce on the OAuth callback.

Do not use pipeline.signature as OAuth state. It is a deterministic MD5 of the pipeline identifiers, not an unpredictable nonce tied to this user's authorization attempt (the tests reuse it across users). An attacker can know the expected state and submit a callback containing a code authorized under the attacker's GitHub account, defeating the OAuth login-CSRF protection and the intended binding to the installing user. Generate a cryptographically random per-attempt state, store it in the session/pipeline, and validate and consume it on callback.

issues.descricao: The new OAuth step's token exchange and user lookup are not wrapped in error handling, so GitHub/network failures surface as 500s instead of the installation-failed page.

comentarios.texto: The token request is executed outside the try block. If GitHub's token endpoint is unavailable or the request fails with a connection/timeout error, safe_urlopen raises before the guarded response parsing is reached, and this new installation step returns an unhandled server error instead of the installation-failed response. Include the request itself in the error handling and handle the relevant transport exceptions.

WHAT: safe_urlopen token exchange and get_user_info() (which calls resp.raise_for_status()) are called with no exception handling. WHY: Any network error, timeout, or non-2xx from GitHub bubbles up as an unhandled exception and 500s the install instead of rendering the invalid-request page. HOW: Wrap the exchange plus get_user_info in try/except and return error() on failure.

safe_urlopen() and get_user_info() are called outside any try/except, so network errors, non-2xx responses, or API failures raise unhandled exceptions instead of returning error(). Wrap the token exchange + user-info fetch in try/except and return error() on failure, matching the handled missing-access_token path.

issues.descricao: When no Integration exists yet for the installation_id the pipeline advances without comparing the OAuth user to the installer, bypassing the new ownership check.

comentarios.texto: The missing Integration branch advances the pipeline without verifying that github_authenticated_user installed the supplied installation_id. When the installation webhook has not created a record, or the local record was deleted, finish_pipeline calls build_integration using app credentials and attaches the installation without checking the OAuth user's access, allowing a user with another account's installation ID to bypass the new ownership check. Fail closed until trusted installer information is available and apply the ownership check before every successful next_step.

The record-absent path advances the pipeline before checking whether the authenticated GitHub user installed this app. Installation IDs arrive from the request, and a missing Integration record (for example before the installation webhook is processed) does not establish ownership. As a result, this path can attach an installation belonging to a different GitHub user despite the new authenticity check. Verify the authenticated user's authorization for the installation before advancing in this branch too, rather than relying on the webhook-created record existing.

When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, the code calls next_step() without comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user to the installer. An attacker can supply an installation_id they do not own before the installation webhook has created the row, and bypass the new verification. Do not skip the check in this branch. Either fail closed, or verify ownership another way, for example by confirming the user can access the installation through the GitHub API.

issues.descricao: The installer check indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] without checking that sender exists, raising KeyError for integrations created without sender metadata.
issues.textoGolden: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

comentarios.texto: integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] is indexed without checking that "sender" exists, so an ACTIVE integration whose metadata has no sender raises KeyError (500) here. metadata["sender"] is only populated when state.get("sender") is set (integration.py:376-377), and the only writer of that state is the installation webhook (webhook.py:202-208); integrations created through the pipeline itself carry no sender (confirmed by installation.py:44 which explicitly guards `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`, and by the pipeline-created integration in test_integration.py:730-743). Previously this branch only bound state and called pipeline.next_step(), so this crash is newly introduced. Fix: guard the lookup, e.g. `if pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != (integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}).get("login"):` and decide the desired fallback when sender is absent.

`integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` can raise KeyError. build_integration (line 376-377) only sets metadata["sender"] when state.get("sender") is truthy, so an existing Integration without a sender entry makes this subscripting throw an unhandled KeyError (500) instead of routing to the intended error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` (and treat a missing sender as a failed verification) so the mismatch/absence case returns error() rather than crashing.

The new ownership check indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] even though GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration omits sender for normal pipeline-created integrations. Reconnecting an existing active integration without an OrganizationIntegration and without webhook-populated sender now raises KeyError and returns a server error rather than an installation failure. Handle missing sender explicitly and return the invalid-installation response when trusted installer metadata is unavailable.

issues.descricao: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

comentarios.texto: First response (installation_id) is overwritten by second response (bad state) with no assertion, so the Integration.DoesNotExist / not-ACTIVE branch in GitHubInstallation is never verified. Keep/assert the first flow through a valid OAuth step to reach the installation check instead of only asserting the OAuth state-mismatch error.

This test no longer verifies the "installation not found" path it exists for. The second GET supplies state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the github pipeline signature (that is the 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 asserted in test_github_setup and reused elsewhere). OAuthLoginView.dispatch (integration.py:412-413) therefore returns error() before GitHubInstallation runs, producing the same generic "Invalid installation request." message and the same failed template via the state-mismatch branch. The Integration.DoesNotExist handling at integration.py:493-498 is never reached, so the test would still pass if that handling were removed or broken. Use the real pipeline state so the request advances into GitHubInstallation, or assert on something that distinguishes the state-mismatch branch from the missing-installation branch.

The replacement assertion no longer verifies that a nonexistent installation is rejected: 'Invalid installation request.' is also returned for a state mismatch, missing access token, or missing authenticated login before GitHubInstallation is reached. This test can therefore pass with installation-not-found handling broken if the callback fails OAuth validation instead. Establish a successful OAuth exchange with the actual pipeline state and verify that the nonexistent installation lookup is reached and rejected, rather than accepting this shared authentication-error message alone.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so the `view` scope satisfies a manage check. WHY: an admin with only a view permission on all groups is treated as able to manage groups, because `requireManage()` backs group creation and update; this is a privilege escalation from read to write. HOW: check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`.

WHAT: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` iterates `findByType("Groups")` and returns `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization resource UUID) as if it were a group id. Per-group resources are created with a random id, name = group id and no type set. WHY: the search and count callers pass the result as `UserModel.GROUPS`, which filters by group id, so users/count and the pagination of user search return wrong results for admins with only per-group view-members/manage-members permissions. The only resource found by type is the all-groups type resource, so per-group grants are never collected. HOW: select group resources by name rather than type (for example, the resources whose name is a group id), use `getName()` as the group id, and pass that same group id to `hasPermission`.

WHAT: `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, and `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns this class. The `GroupRemovedEvent` handler in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. WHY: When `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` and `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` are both enabled, the listener is registered and `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`. Every group deletion then fails with an exception inside the event listener. Before this PR `groups()` fell back to the V1 implementation, so this is a regression for groups. HOW: Make `setPermissionsEnabled` a no-op in V2, or have the listener skip V2, for example by cleaning up V2 group resources instead.

issues.descricao: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as well as MANAGE, so an admin with only view permission on all groups passes manage checks such as group creation.
issues.textoGolden: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

comentarios.texto: The no-arg canManage() returns true when the caller holds only an all-groups VIEW permission (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`), whereas the per-group canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) requires MANAGE. WHAT: a caller with only the view scope on all groups is treated as having manage rights. WHY: canManage()/requireManage() gate group creation and other manage operations (e.g. GroupsResource.addGroup -> auth.groups().requireManage()), so a read-only viewer of all groups can create/manage groups — privilege escalation. HOW: drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() only returns true for MANAGE, aligning it with canManage(GroupModel): `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (line 70) evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), identical to canView() at line 52, so a caller granted only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as a group manager. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) correctly requires only MANAGE, and AdminPermissionsSchema defines MANAGE as the manage scope for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, so the two checks disagree. requireManage() therefore succeeds for read-only administrators, letting them create/update/delete groups, add subgroups and map group roles. Drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() checks MANAGE only.

WHAT: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage on VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). WHY: A caller with only view-all-groups permission passes the manage check, allowing group creation/management reserved for manage. HOW: Check only MANAGE, e.g. hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE).

issues.descricao: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authorization resource id instead of the resource name (the group id) for both the permission check and the returned set, so per-group view-members grants are not resolved and user filtering gets wrong ids.
issues.textoGolden: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authz resource IDs (groupResource.getId()) as group IDs and looks them up via findByName. WHY: Resource names equal group IDs (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId()), so findByName(resourceId) misses and the returned set contains unusable IDs, breaking user search/count filtering by group. HOW: Use groupResource.getName() like V1 does (resource.getName().substring prefix / name) for both the hasPermission lookup and the granted set.

findByType callback passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and granted set, but AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup defines resource name (not UUID) as groupId and hasPermission looks up via findByName(server, groupId). Use groupResource.getName() for both check and granted set, otherwise lookups miss to all-groups fallback and callers receive authz UUIDs instead of group IDs.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses groupResource.getId() for lookup and result collection, but V2 group resources are named with the group ID (resolveGroup returns group.getId()) and hasPermission does findByName. Use groupResource.getName() in both places to evaluate the correct per-group resource and to return actual group IDs.

issues.descricao: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.

comentarios.texto: findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) does not enumerate the specific group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, because that method creates them without setting their type. Consequently, specific VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are omitted from the group IDs used for user counts and database filtering. Assign the Groups type to specific group resources and ensure the all-Groups resource is not treated as a model group.

issues.descricao: The user search filter still requires legacy 'group.resource.<id>' resources, so with V2 group permissions the members of authorized groups are excluded from user searches.

comentarios.texto: The new V2 group permission IDs are passed into a JPA filter that still requires a legacy group.resource.<groupId> authorization resource. JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery checks for that prefixed name, whereas AdminPermissionsSchema creates V2 group resources named only with the group ID, so authorized group members are excluded from user searches even with valid group IDs. Update the database filtering path to support V2 resource naming rather than requiring a legacy V1 resource.

issues.descricao: The new Javadoc for requireManageMembers points to canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers.

comentarios.texto: The javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but this method is the require-variant of canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. The text was copied from requireManageMembership above it. It should reference canManageMembers so the documented contract matches the method name and behavior.

The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should refer to canManageMembers(GroupModel), which is a different check, so the doc misdescribes the method.

Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers (copy-paste). Fix link to {@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)} so the contract describes the method it guards.

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says it returns a Stream though the method returns a Set.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says it returns a 'Stream of IDs', but the method returns Set<String>. Change the @return text to describe a Set of group IDs.
@return says 'Stream of IDs' but method returns Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. Fix doc to 'Set of IDs' to match the signature.

The new @return documentation promises a Stream of IDs, but the method declares Set<String> and both implementations return sets. Describe a set of IDs instead, so the documented return contract matches what callers actually receive.

issues.descricao: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission runs a full permission evaluation for every group resource on each user search and count, costing O(groups) policy evaluations per request.

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission passes getResourceTypeResource's result to policyStore.findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE and 500 on group listing and user search when the Groups type resource is missing.

Removing the canViewGlobal short-circuit from the subgroup and group listings makes an admin with an all-groups V2 grant run one full authorization evaluation per group in the listing instead of a single check.
GroupPermissionEvaluator.canView() Javadoc promises VIEW/MANAGE permission grants access, but the V1 GroupPermissions implementation only checks admin roles.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The check that rejected multiple crypto providers is gone, and DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() 200. WHY: If two of them are on the classpath (for example default and FIPS), the winner depends on ServiceLoader order. The server then silently starts with a possibly non-FIPS provider, and the only trace is a debug log. HOW: Keep failing when the top-ranked providers share the same order value, and only allow a strictly lower-order provider to be ignored.

WHAT: readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, and readInteger and readNext pass it to read(length) without checking. WHY: A malformed signature makes new byte[-1] throw NegativeArraySizeException, not the declared IOException, so callers that catch IOException miss it. HOW: Throw an IOException in readLength (or in the callers) when the length is negative.

issues.descricao: concatenatedRSToASN1DER encodes r and s into two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances before re-encoding them in the return statement.
issues.textoGolden: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: the two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls allocate encoders and encode rBigInteger/sBigInteger, but their results are discarded — the returned DER comes entirely from the expression at lines 117-121, which re-encodes the same BigIntegers. These two statements have no effect and should be removed (they are a leftover from an earlier formulation).

Remove these two discarded encoder writes. Each allocates an encoder and encodes a BigInteger, but neither result participates in the returned signature; lines 119–120 repeat both writes on fresh encoders. This performs redundant encoding and allocations on every concatenated-signature conversion.

The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` encode values and discard the results. The return expression re-encodes the same values, so these lines are dead computation left over from a copy-paste or refactor. Remove them.

issues.descricao: order() is added to CryptoProvider as an abstract method, breaking source and binary compatibility for existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations.
issues.textoGolden: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

comentarios.texto: order() was added as an abstract method to the public CryptoProvider interface. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now invokes order() on every ServiceLoader-discovered CryptoProvider via Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order). Any CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface (an external or separately built provider jar on the classpath) will throw AbstractMethodError at detection time, i.e. during AuthzClient.create()/server bootstrap, before any provider is usable. Giving order() a default implementation (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }) avoids the binary-incompatibility.

issues.descricao: detectProvider no longer fails when several crypto providers are present; with Default, FIPS and Elytron all at order 200, ties are resolved by classpath order and a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS provider.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: detectProvider sorts by order() reversed and silently picks index 0, removing the previous multiple-providers error. WHY: Default/FIPS/Elytron all return order 200, so ambiguous classpath (e.g. default+FIPS) now nondeterministically picks one by ServiceLoader order instead of failing fast, risking wrong FIPS vs non-FIPS crypto. HOW: only auto-ignore lower-order providers; throw when the top two have equal order().

Reject ambiguous highest-priority providers rather than silently taking the first. Both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider return order 200 in this PR, so when both are present the stable sort leaves the decision to ServiceLoader discovery order. A deployment expecting FIPS can therefore initialize the ordinary Bouncy Castle provider without an error; previously this mixed classpath failed closed. Preserve the error for tied highest-priority providers (or require an explicit security-mode/provider choice), while still allowing the lower-priority authz-client fallback.

detectProvider() no longer fails fast when multiple CryptoProviders are present and instead silently picks the first after sorting by order() descending. All Keycloak providers return the same order (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200), so a tie between two providers is broken by the non-deterministic ServiceLoader iteration order rather than the intended priority. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException forcing the classpath to be corrected; now a deployment with two provider jars (exactly the 'multiple providers on classpath' scenario this PR enables) can silently select the unintended provider — e.g. a non-FIPS/strict provider when FIPS is required — with no error. Use a stable tie-breaker (delegate to the provider name/type) or reject equal top orders instead of relying on ServiceLoader order.

issues.descricao: Claims a wrong-length JOSE signature causes an unchecked exception in concatenatedRSToASN1DER; verifiers catch it and report verification failure, as with the existing providers.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature without validating signature.length==signLength. WHY: short JOSE input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and long input is silently truncated to signLength, breaking the ECDSACryptoProvider contract (IOException on malformed) used by verifier contexts. HOW: check length upfront and throw IOException.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER never validates signature.length == signLength before System.arraycopy(signature,0,r,1,len) / (signature,len,s,1,len). A short JWS signature throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException, breaking verification on attacker-controlled input. Validate length and throw IOException.

issues.descricao: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with the same default P-256 key, so the converter is never tested with real P-384 or P-521 signatures.

comentarios.texto: Single default EC keypair reused for ES256/ES384/ES512: testES384/testES512 names claim larger curves but body signs with the same P-256 key and only pads to larger signLength, so full-width 384/521-bit handling is never exercised. Generate a per-algorithm keypair with the correct curve (e.g. secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) before signing.

Every case generates a default EC key rather than a key on the curve associated with the named algorithm. On the standard JDK this is P-256, so testES384 and testES512 just pad P-256 signature components to larger lengths. A converter that discards nonzero high bytes beyond 32 bytes would still pass all three cases. Initialize the key generator with the appropriate curve per case (P-256, P-384, and P-521) so the larger-component conversions are actually tested.

Generate a key on the curve corresponding to each tested algorithm rather than using the provider's default EC curve for all three tests. On the standard JDK this generates a P-256 key even for testES384 and testES512, so those tests merely pad P-256 integers to larger output lengths and never exercise actual P-384/P-521 signature encoding (including P-521's long-form sequence length).

issues.descricao: The test only checks a round trip between the two new converters and never verifies the re-encoded DER against the original signature or with Signature.verify, so mutually consistent bugs go undetected.

comentarios.texto: Tautological round-trip assertion: rsConcat2 is derived from rsConcat via encode+decode that are inverses if self-consistent, so assertArrayEquals(rsConcat,rsConcat2) passes even if both directions are wrong. Verify against external oracle: Signature.initVerify + verify(asn1Des) and/or compare rsConcat to expected split, not just to itself.

The test only checks self-consistency: it asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(g(asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign))) == asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign), i.e. that concatenatedRSToASN1DER is a right inverse of asn1derToConcatenatedRS. It never compares against the original DER `sign`, never verifies the ECDSA signature, and never asserts the emvider output is canonical DER. Because the decoder it reads back with (ASN1Decoder.readLength) accepts non-canonical long-form lengths (e.g. 0x81) and validates only tag numbers, a regression in ASN1Encoder.writeLength that always emitted long form would still round-trip and the test would still pass, even though the produced signature would no longer be valid DER and would be rejected by the Keycloak server / a JDK Signature.verify. Assert the encoded signature is valid DER (e.g. verify it with a JDK Signature, or compare asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign) against a known-good width-padded r||s and assert its length equals algorithm.getSignatureLength()).

The assertion only establishes agreement between the two new conversion routines, not correctness of the converted signature. For example, swapping r and s in both routines makes this entire round trip pass, although the DER result no longer verifies the signed data. Verify `asn1Des` with the public key and original data (or compare against an independently specified encoding) so mutually compensating conversion defects fail the test.

issues.descricao: getBouncyCastleProvider in AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns the JDK default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle, contrary to the CryptoProvider contract.
ASN1Decoder.readInteger accepts constructed INTEGER tags because it only masks the low tag bits, so malformed DER is parsed as valid.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `totalPages` is floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overcounts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members and limit 50 gives 2 pages). WHY: `showingLast` then never becomes true on the real last page, so "next" navigates to an empty page and the pager shows a nonexistent page. HOW: use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

WHAT: `members` now defaults to 50 rows for every group, but the public group members template (`group/members.hbs`) has no paging controls. WHY: before this PR only automatic groups were truncated, so non-automatic groups with more than 50 members now silently show only the first 50 on the public page. HOW: add paging to the public members view, or raise the default limit.

WHAT: `limit` and `offset` come straight from request params with no cap or lower bound, and the limit is now applied to every group. WHY: a public caller can pass a huge `limit` and force loading and serializing the whole group in one request, and a negative `limit` or `offset` produces a database error (500). HOW: clamp `limit` to a sane range and `offset` to >= 0.

WHAT: `removeMember` reloads with `findMembers()` at the old offset. WHY: removing the only member on the last page (e.g. 51 members, offset 50) makes the new offset equal to the new total, so the server returns an empty page and the UI shows an empty list on a page that no longer exists. HOW: after the reload, if offset >= total and offset > 0, step back one page and reload.

issues.descricao: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
issues.textoGolden: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

comentarios.texto: totalPages (and currentPage) use `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 → reports 2 pages although only 1 exists). This leaves `showingLast` false on the real last page, so 'next' navigates to an empty page at offset=user_count. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and compute currentPage consistently) to get the correct page count.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 for user_count=50, limit=50, although 50 members occupy exactly one page. Correct it to `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`. Effect: for a group whose member count is a multiple of the page size, totalPages is one too high, showingLast remains false so the 'next' link stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to a phantom empty page.

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, on a full last page `showingLast` is false, so the `next` action stays enabled and advances `offset` to `user_count`, rendering an empty page labeled as the last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero-member guard) so the count matches the real number of pages.

issues.descricao: Several Group model functions (findMembers, destroy, userCountDisplay) return a value on some paths and undefined on others, triggering consistent-return lint warnings.
issues.textoGolden: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

issues.descricao: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

comentarios.texto: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

issues.descricao: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.

comentarios.texto: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

issues.descricao: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.

comentarios.texto: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

issues.descricao: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#remove destroy path. WHY: bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks and primary_group_id cleanup done in destroy_deletions, leaving stale membership side-effects (e.g. dangling primary_group_id). HOW: load the User and call group.remove(user).

Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

issues.descricao: The remove_member spec issues a PUT request although the route only maps DELETE to remove_member, so the test uses a verb never routed in production.
issues.textoGolden: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

comentarios.texto: This example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the PR maps `remove_member` only to DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT on that path routes to `groups#add_members`. Controller specs bypass the router, so the example still lands on `remove_member` and passes regardless — it would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired to the wrong action, leaving the newly introduced verb/action pairing untested. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member`, as the sibling example at line 125 already does.

The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. It exercises the action with a verb that is never routed in production. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` so the test matches the real request.

issues.descricao: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
`add_members` runs one User query per username; load all users with a single `User.where(username: ...)` query.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `scheduleSMS` returns undefined when the user or team is SMS-locked, and it throws on rate-limit or transient Twilio errors. Both paths now increment `retryCount`. WHY: after about 3 cron runs, reminders hit by a temporary lock, rate limit, or Twilio outage are permanently deleted, though they would previously have been retried until their date. HOW: increment `retryCount` only for permanent failures such as an invalid number, or distinguish the locked and rate-limit cases and skip the increment for them.

WHAT: The `update` inside the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. WHY: if the update throws (row already deleted or DB error), the exception escapes the loop, so the remaining reminders in the batch are skipped and the cron returns a 500. HOW: wrap the update in try/catch, or use `updateMany`, which does not throw when no row matches.

WHAT: The `retryCount > 1` delete branch is not scoped to `method: SMS`, so it matches reminders of every method. WHY: any current or future non-SMS reminder with `retryCount > 1` would be deleted by the SMS cron. HOW: move the retryCount condition inside the SMS filter.

issues.descricao: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
issues.textoGolden: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: retryCount is incremented with a read-value computed at the start of the run (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic increment. WHY: if two cron invocations overlap (or the same reminder is processed twice before the write commits), both read the same retryCount and both write N+1, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can loop forever without ever reaching the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold. HOW: use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` so the increment is atomic (the initial read value is then irrelevant).

`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write of the value fetched at the top of the handler, not an atomic increment. Two overlapping cron runs both read the same retryCount and both write the same +1, losing an update, so failed reminders can be retried indefinitely and never reach the `gt: 1` deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of computing from the stale in-memory value (same issue in the else branch at lines 179-186).

Retry counts are assigned from the stale findMany snapshot instead of incremented atomically, both here and in the catch branch. Two overlapping cron requests can each fail scheduling the same reminder with retryCount zero and both write one, so two failed attempts do not reach the deletion threshold and additional attempts are scheduled. Use Prisma's atomic retryCount increment operation in both failure branches.

issues.descricao: The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.
issues.textoGolden: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

comentarios.texto: The comment "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" no longer describes the deleteMany below it. After this change the query also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, and that OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so non-SMS (email) reminders with retryCount > 1 are now deleted too. Update the comment (or add the missing SMS filter to the retryCount branch) so the prose matches what the code actually deletes.
The deleteMany OR clause deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method.

The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, unlike the first branch (`method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`). Because `retryCount` is a generic column on WorkflowReminder used by all reminder methods, this deleteMany now permanently deletes every reminder of ANY method (including EMAIL) whose retryCount exceeds 1, even though this cron is only supposed to clean up SMS reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to this branch (or scope the whole where to SMS) so non-SMS reminders are never destroyed.

issues.descricao: The cleanup comment describes only past-date SMS deletion and omits the new retryCount > 1 deletion branch.

comentarios.texto: Update the cleanup comment to describe the new retry-exhaustion deletion branch. It currently says this deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose date has passed, but this OR branch also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, including future-dated reminders and without an SMS restriction. The comment now misrepresents the scope of this destructive operation.

Stale comment: line 28 says 'delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date' but the new OR clause also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method or date. Update the comment to describe both branches.

issues.descricao: The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the catch block performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` while handling the scheduling error. WHY: if this write itself rejects (e.g. the row was concurrently removed, or a transient DB error), the rejection is not caught and escapes the for-loop, aborting the whole cron run so all remaining reminders go unprocessed. HOW: wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch (log and continue) so a failure to record the retry does not abort processing of the remaining reminders.

This new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` sits inside the catch block, which is NOT protected by any try/catch. If this update throws (e.g. the reminder was already removed by the `deleteMany` at the top of the file during a concurrent run -> Prisma P2025, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the `for` loop and rejects the handler, so all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the cron request fails. Previously the catch only did `console.log`, so a single bad reminder never aborted the batch and the endpoint always returned 200. Wrap this update in its own try/catch (or `updateMany`/catch-and-log) so a failed retry-count write cannot take down the whole scheduling run.

The new database update inside catch can itself throw when a reminder has been deleted during scheduling. Booking cancellation deletes reminders through handleCancelBooking and deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so a concurrent cancellation followed by a scheduling error now rejects the entire cron handler and prevents the remaining reminders from being processed. Use an updateMany filtered by the reminder ID to tolerate an already-deleted row, and guard errors from retry bookkeeping so they do not escape the per-reminder error handler.

issues.descricao: Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The catch block unconditionally increments retryCount for any exception (profile/bookerUrl/templating/rate-limit/Twilio outage). WHY: Two consecutive cron runs with a transient global failure increment every pending SMS reminder to 2 and the startup deleteMany then wipes the entire future SMS queue, not just permanently-invalid numbers. HOW: Only increment on permanent scheduleSMS failure, or distinguish transient errors from terminal ones before counting toward deletion.

issues.descricao: The new OR arm on retryCount has no supporting index, so the cleanup delete can no longer be fully served by the existing index and may scan the table.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the deleteMany WHERE now uses `OR` between `(method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now)` and `retryCount > 1`, but WorkflowReminder has no index on the newly added retryCount column. WHY: Postgres cannot satisfy a two-way OR using the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index and will fall back to a sequential scan of the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation, turning a previously indexed delete into a full table scan as the table grows. HOW: add an index on retryCount (or restructure so each branch is index-usable), then re-check the query plan.

issues.descricao: The retryCount increment update is duplicated in the else branch and the catch block.

comentarios.texto: The retryCount increment is duplicated in the else-branch and catch.

issues.descricao: SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.
retryCount is not incremented when a reminder has no message or no sendTo number, so such reminders are reprocessed on every cron run until their scheduled date.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil, and `tu.notification_level` is then called on it. WHY: a user who has no `topic_users` row for the topic (for example one notified through category watching, or following an old email link) gets NoMethodError and an HTTP 500 instead of being unsubscribed. HOW: guard against nil, or go through `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when it is missing.

WHAT: the GET `unsubscribe` action steps the notification level down on every request: watching or tracking goes to regular, and regular goes to muted. WHY: a page reload, a second click, or a mail-client or security-scanner prefetch of the emailed link silently escalates the user from regular to muted, so they miss all later replies. The GET also changes state without confirmation. HOW: make the action idempotent, for example by setting one deterministic target level such as regular. Alternatively, have GET only render the page and make the change in a POST/PUT triggered by the user.

WHAT: the notification level is written directly with `tu.save!` instead of through `TopicUser.change`. WHY: `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated, and no `/topic/:id` MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published. The notification button on the unsubscribe page and other open tabs can then show the old state. HOW: call `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: new_level)`.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use.
